Management effectiveness in executing asset sales: broken/insufficient [D03, D05]

final.remaining_skew: Significant value resides in the royalty stream, but capital allocation remains inefficient; upside dependent on forced liquidation [D05, D06]
final.next_catalyst_and_timing: Appointment of independent directors or announcement of a definitive agreement for asset sale [D07]
asks_if_escalating: Immediate cessation of all non-essential R&D spend
Full divestiture of all commercial assets rather than piecemeal sales
Commitment to return proceeds to shareholders via buybacks or special dividends

drivers.driver: Management’s piecemeal approach to asset sales is suboptimal and destroys value through overhead and tax leakage [D05, D06].
The clinical failure of Nuvion confirms that the R&D pipeline is a value-destroying use of capital rather than a growth engine [D02, D03].
The company trades at a persistent discount to the sum-of-the-parts of its royalty assets due to capital misallocation [D06].
As an Era A/B holding, public escalation is our standard tool to force accountability when a strategic review is underway but moving too slowly [D07].

final.memo:
PDL BioPharma is a classic example of an asset with a valuable, recurring royalty stream being obscured by the heavy cost and poor performance of an integrated biotech business [D01, D06]. Our original thesis focused on the inherent value of the royalty portfolio; however, management’s insistence on sustaining a clinical-development engine—despite the recent failure of the Nuvion trial—continues to bleed cash and depress equity value [D02, D03, D05].

Management has announced an intent to sell commercial assets, but we have no faith in their ability to execute a process that optimizes value for shareholders [D03, D07]. A piecemeal sale strategy only ensures the survival of redundant overhead and creates tax leakage that we, as owners, will not tolerate [D05, D06]. The time for polite, private dialogue has passed [D08].

We are moving to ESCALATE because the current market price does not reflect the underlying royalty value, and management’s pace of change is glacial [D04, D07]. We intend to make our demands public: stop the empire-building, divest the remaining non-core assets in their entirety, and return the capital to the owners [D05]. We are not interested in waiting for a future that may never materialize under the current leadership [D05, D07].
